images.alt_grc: ὁ Λύσις γέρων ἤδη τοῖς τοῦ υἱοῦ παισὶ βιβλίον ἀναγιγνώσκει.
images.alt_en: About 370 BC. An old, white-bearded Lysis sits on a stool in the courtyard of a house in Kydathenaion, unrolling a papyrus scroll; two grandchildren (a boy of about ten and a younger girl) sit at his feet in the evening light. A lamp and a painted cup from the family workshop on a small table.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Κῦρος μετὰ τῶν ὁπλιτῶν καὶ τοῦ Τισσαφέρνους ἀναβαίνει.
images.alt_en: The scene of the book: the young Persian prince Cyrus on horseback, in Persian dress, riding inland with the satrap Tissaphernes beside him and a small column of Greek hoplites with round shields behind, led by their commander Xenias.
A Persian palace hall: King Artaxerxes on his throne; Cyrus held by two guards; the queen mother Parysatis kneeling and pleading for him while Tissaphernes looks on.

images.alt_grc: ἡ μικρὰ κόρη ἐρωτᾷ· «τί εἶδον οἱ Ἕλληνες;»
images.alt_en: Old Lysis reading the scroll again; his granddaughter leans forward eagerly asking a question, her hand raised; through the doorway a glimpse of the sea-blue sky.

images.alt_grc: οἱ ὀπισθοφύλακες τοὺς πολεμίους φεύγοντας διώκουσιν.
images.alt_en: A column of weary Greek soldiers with pack animals climbing a mountain path in spring; at the rear the rearguard fights off local tribesmen; smoke rises from the burning land behind them; wicker shields and shaggy rawhide shields lie captured on the ground.

The top of Mount Theches: soldiers running up the ridge, arms raised, shouting; far below and beyond, the Black Sea shines on the horizon. Xenophon on horseback with the cavalry rides up from the rear.
Old Lysis takes a second scroll from a wooden chest; its label tag reads ΚΡΙΤΩΝ; the grandchildren watch.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Κρίτων παρὰ τῷ Σωκράτει καθεύδοντι σιγῇ κάθηται.
images.alt_en: Before dawn in a bare prison room lit by one lamp: Socrates, an old man with a snub nose, asleep on a plank bed; his friend Crito, also old and well dressed, sits silently beside him watching.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Σωκράτης καὶ ὁ Κρίτων διαλέγονται.
images.alt_en: Socrates, now awake and sitting up, speaks calmly to Crito, who leans forward anxiously; grey dawn light through a high barred window; a guard dozes by the door.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Σωκράτης καὶ ὁ Γλαύκων εἰς Πειραιᾶ κατέβησαν.
images.alt_en: The Piraeus at a festival: Socrates and a young man (Glaucon) watch two processions, Athenians and Thracians in patterned cloaks and fox-skin caps, passing a small shrine.

images.alt_grc: ὁ παῖς τοῦ ἱματίου τοῦ Σωκράτους λαμβάνεται.
images.alt_en: On the road back towards the city walls: a slave boy runs up behind Socrates and tugs at his cloak; in the distance Polemarchus waves from among a group of young men.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Πολέμαρχος καὶ οἱ φίλοι τὸν Σωκράτη μένειν κελεύουσιν.
images.alt_en: Polemarchus, Adeimantus, Niceratus and others surround Socrates and Glaucon, laughing and pointing back to the Piraeus; Socrates smiles and gives in.

images.alt_grc: οἱ φύλακες τοῦ βασιλέως τῶν Περσῶν.
images.alt_en: Glazed-brick frieze of Persian royal guards (the 'Immortals') with spears and bows, from the palace of Darius I at Susa, c. 510 BC (Louvre; museum photograph, CC).
View from the mountains above Trabzon (ancient Trapezus) down to the Black Sea coast (landscape photograph, CC).
Marble portrait head of Socrates, Roman copy of a Greek original of the fourth century BC (museum photograph, CC).
Votive relief from the Piraeus, c. 400–375 BC (British Museum): the Thracian goddess Bendis receives a team of young torch-racers and their trainers (museum photograph, CC).
